record.paper_title: Methods for Computing All Roots of a Polynomial Simultaneously - Known Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Global convergence of the simultaneous Euler-Chebyshev method
record.original_question: For the simultaneous Euler-Chebyshev method for computing all zeros of a polynomial, prove or refute that the iteration is globally convergent outside a subset of the starting space of measure zero, and describe that exceptional set for arbitrary degree n.

evidence.quote: Problem K2. (Kyurkchiev [14]) Show that the Euler - Chebyshev method is globally convergent outside of a set of measure zero in the starting space and describe this set, for arbitrary n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p(z) be a complex polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 with n pairwise distinct zeros ζ_1, …, ζ_n ∈ ℂ. The simultaneous Euler–Chebyshev iteration is the map T : U ⊂ ℂ^n → ℂ^n defined componentwise, for a vector x = (x_1, …, x_n) of pairwise distinct approximations to the zeros, by

  T_i(x) = x_i − (p(x_i)/p'(x_i)) · ( 1 + (1/2) · A_i(x) + (1/2) · A_i(x)^2 ),

where
  A_i(x) = (p(x_i)/p'(x_i)) · Σ_{j ≠ i} 1/(x_i − x_j),

and the iterates are x^{(k+1)} = T(x^{(k)}), starting from x^{(0)} ∈ ℂ^n with all components pairwise distinct and away from the critical set of T.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following statement, and in the affirmative case give an explicit description of the exceptional set:

  For every n ≥ 2, the simultaneous Euler–Chebyshev iteration is globally convergent — in the sense that the sequence x^{(k)} converges to a permutation of (ζ_1, …, ζ_n) — for all initial vectors x^{(0)} ∈ ℂ^n outside a subset E ⊂ ℂ^n of (2n-dimensional Lebesgue) measure zero. Identify and characterize the exceptional set E for arbitrary degree n.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches return results on local convergence and accelerated variants of Chebyshev-/Euler-Chebyshev-type simultaneous root-finding methods (e.g., Iliev–Kyurkchiev, Proinov and collaborators), but no source establishes global convergence almost everywhere of the simultaneous Euler–Chebyshev method or characterizes its exceptional set for arbitrary degree n. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Local convergence of Chebyshev-like method for simultaneous finding polynomial zeros
status_evidence.snippet: Studies local (not global) convergence of Chebyshev-like simultaneous methods.
status_evidence.claim: Available results address only local convergence.

status_evidence.title: On a generalization of the Euler-Chebyshev method for simultaneous extraction of only a part of all roots of polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Generalization aimed at extracting part of the roots; no global a.e. convergence proof for the full simultaneous Euler–Chebyshev iteration.
status_evidence.claim: No global convergence theorem outside a measure-zero set is provided.

status_evidence.title: Families of high-order simultaneous methods with several corrections
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) work on simultaneous root-finders giving local/semilocal convergence for Chebyshev-type families.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature still treats local/semilocal convergence rather than global a.e. convergence.
